predecessors.name: Duchy of Benevento
predecessors.text: Salerno, where Siconulf was proclaimed prince after Sicard's murder in 839; the rest of the principality was assigned only in the 851 division

successors.name: Norman Italy
successors.text: the whole principality, which after 1077 'was completely merged into the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria'

ledger.x: 840: Siconulf is proclaimed prince at Salerno.
840-851: the civil war.
851: Louis II divides the principality.
851: the division gives Salerno the southern lands.
861: Capua breaks away.

c. 968: the Byzantines form the Theme of Lucania. 'established probably c. 968, under emperor Nikephoros II Phokas'; it 'corresponds roughly to modern Basilicata'. The page does not say the land came from Salerno or mention Cosenza; the region is Cliopatria's 970 loss. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: confidence lowered…
978: Pandulf II of the Capuan house succeeds.
981: Amalfi takes Salerno.
983: the Salernitans choose their own prince.
May 1038: Guaimar IV becomes Prince of Capua.
April 1039: Guaimar IV becomes Duke of Amalfi.
1040: 'The Prince of Salerno Guaimar IV took control of Benevento in 1040'.
June 1040: Guaimar takes Gaeta.
After October 1041: Gaeta slips away.
1043: the Normans acclaim Guaimar.
1047: Henry III undoes Guaimar's work.
1047: Henry III 'deprived Guaimar of his title over Apulia and Calabria' and took Aversa and Melfi under his own suzerainty; in 1048 Guaimar 'recaptured the allegiance of Aversa'.
1047 on the bridge: the Guaimar page says only that in 1047 'The emperor also besieged Benevento'; the Benevento page gives no end to the 1040 hold.

1052: Guaimar IV is assassinated in the harbour of Salerno (2, 3 or 4 June, the sources differ) and his dukedom of Amalfi, held 1039-1052, ends with him; Gisulf II succeeds as prince, 'whom the Normans put under their protection'.
13 December 1076: Salerno submits.
May 1077: the citadel falls.
1077: the Lombard principality ends.

wars.name: Civil war of the Beneventan succession (Radelchis I against Siconulf)
wars.outcome: Louis II divided the principality in 851 into Benevento and Salerno; Salerno received Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza and Sarno, and Capua.

wars.name: Conrad II's expedition to Capua
wars.outcome: Conrad II, invited south by Guaimar IV, besieged Capua and gave the principality to Guaimar in May 1038; Henry III reversed this in 1047.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Salerno
wars.outcome: Robert Guiscard took the city (December 1076) and the citadel (May 1077); the principality was merged into the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.

certainty.note: The 851 division of Louis II named the gastaldates assigned to each prince but fixed no surveyed line; the Basilicata frontier with the Byzantine theme and the Capuan frontier were never delimited on the pages opened.
